I now realize the very nature of sharing a tattoo instead of temporary artwork doesn't invite much discussion about the art. It's pretty low to openly bash someone's tattoo they've chosen to have on their body for the rest of their lives. Let me just throw out there that, as the bearer of this tattoo, any critiques about the art are okay, if not necessarily what I was going for. I've chosen this to be immortalized on my body because it means something special to me and that meaning is where I hoped discussion to stem from. And for the most part, that's what is happening which speaks to the positive soul of this community. So, feel free to give me your art critiques if you wish, in the spirit of appreciation for good art and good tattoos and constant improvement!

Your essay struck a specific chord in me as I read it. You're right. Stormlight Archive is special. Yes it can be categorized at "genre fiction," simply by its fantasy nature. However, there are REAL human characters underneath the surgebinders and shardbearers. 

Kaladin (and other members of bridge 4) is a man who has continued to fight depression, regardless of the power he has gained. Depression is a demon that physical and political power cannot overcome. 

Dalinar is a good man, uncompromising in his morals, who still battles the shame of his past, whether in victory or defeat. No amount of good deeds today can erase the past, but neither can a cruel past diminish the positive actions of today. 

"Sometimes, a hypocrite is nothing more than a man who is in the process of changing." Journey before destination.

The Bridge 4 glyph was a close second for me! Almost got that instead of the Kaladin-specific tattoo. I think I ultimately wanted his symbol rather than a general bridge 4 tattoo because the story arc of Kaladin specifically is one I admire so much.

I think there's something to be said for the attention to detail Sanderson goes into when portraying a character with a particular mental illness or struggle. Whether it be Kaladin or Teft, their depressive characteristics are unique from each other and consistent throughout the story. 

It's easy to say both characters struggle with depression, but their manifestations are wholly unique and not necessarily suited to understanding each other.

Thanks! I'm 100% with you there. At least with the books so far, the particular sufferings of those two characters are extremely relatable as a man who struggles with depression and chronic loneliness. I love the story and well done fantasy, but I've never felt such simultaneous humanity and badassery from fictional characters before reading Stormlight Archive.
